subject: Follow-up: NovaPay streaming JSON truncation — triage summary
messages:
From: Alex Kim <a.kim@novapay.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent streaming response truncation (JSON keys missing)

Hi Vanessa / Dev,

We're seeing a handful of requests where the streamed completion ends with a truncated JSON object — specifically keys like 'customer_id' or 'items' are missing at the end of the payload. This happens ~2–3 times per 10k requests and only affects our streaming integration. Non-streaming (single response) requests look fine.

Example: 2026-12-18T08:56:23 UTC, request id np-7742. We attached a small sample payload and a client log excerpt. Can you confirm this is on your side or something in our streaming parser?

We rely on the stream to incrementally parse and save partial results; when the final token set is missing keys our downstream jobs fail. We're happy to share access to our staging environment if helpful.

Thanks,
Alex
Platform Engineer — NovaPay

Attachments: novapay_sample_payloads.json (json), client_stream_log_excerpt.txt (txt)

Subject: Re: Intermittent streaming response truncation (JSON keys missing)

Hi Alex — thanks for the report and sample. I'm looping in Dev from infra to run reproductions and collect traces. A couple quick clarifying asks so we can prioritize:

- Is the problem always the last token(s) missing, or do you sometimes see keys truncated in the middle of the JSON stream?
- Does the client reassemble the stream verbatim, or do you run any client-side trimming/line-buffering on receipt?
- Can you confirm whether you saw the issue with both the hosted redwood-api region us-west-2 and us-east-1 (if you have traffic in both)?

We'll attempt to reproduce with your sample payloads and return a timeline by EOD PT. If we can access a staging endpoint, please share a short-lived key.

—Vanessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Alex Kim <a.kim@novapay.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent streaming response truncation (JSON keys missing)

Hi Alex, Vanessa — I ran a reproduction using the sample payloads Alex provided and a small harness that mimics NovaPay's streaming consumer. Summary of findings:

- I replayed ~10k requests at the same token lengths and sequence sizes. I could not reproduce truncated JSON emitted by our runtime; in all cases the stream ended with a complete JSON payload and a valid closing brace.
- I collected an internal trace for request id np-7742 and attached the redwood trace (redwood_trace_20261218.log). The server shows a normal completion and no connection reset or runtime OOM.
- I then inspected a client capture you sent (client_stream_log_excerpt.txt). The client appears to implement a small line-buffer that flushes on newline boundaries and then parses incrementally; when the stream sends tokens without a trailing newline, the client-side parser sometimes writes the fragment and treats the next streamed chunk as a fresh JSON object, resulting in dropped key association.

Preliminary conclusion: no evidence of server-side truncation; likely client-side streaming assembly behavior. To be safe, please try the following on your staging consumer:

1) Accept the stream until the server emits the final event (we provide a streaming 'done' marker) instead of flushing on newline.
2) Buffer and append token chunks before JSON parsing, or use the SDK's streaming helper which concatenates chunks for you.

If you share a staging endpoint and short-lived key I can run a coordinated test while watching server traces. If you prefer, I can also deploy a small instrumented proxy to help prove the hypothesis.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_trace_20261218.log (log)

From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <a.kim@novapay.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 17:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent streaming response truncation (JSON keys missing) — Triage complete

Hi Alex — quick closure note from Redwood after the triage: thank you for the sample payloads and logs. Based on Dev's reproductions and the traces we reviewed, we did not find any runtime-level truncation or network-level resets originating from Redwood for the recorded requests.

Action items and recommendations:
- NovaPay engineering: adjust the streaming consumer to buffer token chunks until you receive the stream completion marker (or use the official SDK stream helper). This change eliminated the symptom for our staged replay.
- Redwood: we published the internal traces (link in related_links) and attached triage_notes_20261220.md summarizing steps taken. If you prefer, we can run a joint test with a staging key — ping me a time window and we will shadow the requests.
- We are monitoring production traffic for a week with an alert that will flag any server-side connection anomalies; we'll loop back if anything new is found.

Because the evidence points to client-side parsing behavior and we've provided reproducible mitigations, we're closing this triage as "not confirmed on Redwood". If you continue to see missing keys after applying the buffering change, re-open this thread and we'll escalate to a deeper network trace.

Thanks — open to a call if helpful.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
